requirements.quote:
The header protection algorithm uses both the header protection key
   and a sample of the ciphertext from the packet Payload field.
requirements.condition: When applying the header protection algorithm
requirements.required_behavior: Use the header protection key as an algorithm input.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply header protection without the header protection key.
requirements.why_checkable: The header-protection invocation can be instrumented or reproduced to verify that it consumes the derived header protection key.

requirements.quote:
The header protection algorithm uses both the header protection key
   and a sample of the ciphertext from the packet Payload field.
requirements.condition: When applying the header protection algorithm
requirements.required_behavior: Use a ciphertext sample taken from the packet Payload field as an algorithm input.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use plaintext or bytes outside the packet Payload field as the sample source.
requirements.why_checkable: For a known packet layout, the bytes passed to header protection can be compared with the ciphertext bytes at the required Payload position.

requirements.quote: The same number of bytes are always sampled
requirements.condition: When sampling ciphertext for a selected header protection algorithm
requirements.required_behavior: Sample the fixed number of bytes required by that algorithm for every packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Vary the sample length based on the encoded Packet Number field length.
requirements.why_checkable: Sample lengths can be recorded across packets with different packet-number encodings and compared with the algorithm's required sample length.

requirements.quote:
The
   sample of ciphertext is taken starting from an offset of 4 bytes
   after the start of the Packet Number field.
requirements.condition: When locating the ciphertext sample for header protection
requirements.required_behavior: Set the sample start to four bytes after the start of the Packet Number field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Base the sample start on the actual encoded Packet Number field length.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected sample offset can be compared directly with packet_number_offset + 4 for packet numbers of every encoded length.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST discard packets that are not long enough to contain
   a complete sample.
requirements.condition: When a received packet is too short to contain the complete header protection sample
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Attempt header protection removal using a partial or out-of-bounds sample.
requirements.error_behavior: Discard the undersized packet rather than processing it further.
requirements.why_checkable: Truncated packets can be injected and the endpoint observed to ensure they are discarded without a partial-sample header-protection operation.

requirements.quote:
packets are
   padded so that the combined lengths of the encoded packet number and
   protected payload is at least 4 bytes longer than the sample required
   for header protection.
requirements.condition: When constructing a packet that will use header protection
requirements.required_behavior: Pad the packet until encoded_packet_number_length + protected_payload_length is at least sample_length + 4 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Emit a protected packet whose combined encoded packet number and protected payload is shorter than sample_length + 4 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded packet-number and protected-payload lengths can be measured and checked against the exact inequality.

requirements.quote:
The cipher suites defined in [TLS13] -- other
   than TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256, for which a header protection scheme
   is not defined in this document -- have 16-byte expansions
requirements.condition: When using a TLS 1.3 cipher suite other than TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256
requirements.why_checkable: For packets protected with each covered cipher suite, ciphertext length can be compared with plaintext length to verify the 16-byte expansion.

requirements.quote:
The cipher suites defined in [TLS13] -- other
   than TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256, for which a header protection scheme
   is not defined in this document -- have 16-byte expansions and
   16-byte header protection samples.
requirements.condition: When using a TLS 1.3 cipher suite other than TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another header protection sample length for the covered cipher suites.
requirements.why_checkable: The sample passed to the header protection function can be measured and asserted to contain exactly 16 bytes.

requirements.quote:
TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256, for which a header protection scheme
   is not defined in this document
requirements.required_behavior: Apply an appropriate header protection scheme.
requirements.why_checkable: This chunk explicitly states that it does not define the necessary scheme and supplies no required fallback, rejection, or error behavior, so conformance behavior cannot be determined from this evidence.

requirements.quote:
This results in needing at least
   3 bytes of frames in the unprotected payload if the packet number is
   encoded on a single byte
requirements.condition: When using a covered 16-byte-expansion cipher suite and encoding the packet number in one byte
requirements.required_behavior: Include at least 3 bytes of frames in the unprotected payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Construct the packet with fewer than 3 bytes of frames before protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame bytes can be counted before protection and checked against the stated three-byte minimum.

requirements.quote:
or 2 bytes of frames for a 2-byte packet
   number encoding.
requirements.condition: When using a covered 16-byte-expansion cipher suite and encoding the packet number in two bytes
requirements.required_behavior: Include at least 2 bytes of frames in the unprotected payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Construct the packet with fewer than 2 bytes of frames before protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame bytes can be counted before protection and checked against the stated two-byte minimum.

requirements.required_behavior: Take sample_length bytes from the packet beginning at sample_offset as the header protection sample.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Take the sample from another range of packet bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected sample bytes can be compared byte-for-byte with the specified packet slice.

requirements.condition: When calculating the Packet Number field offset of a short-header packet
requirements.why_checkable: For short-header packets with varying connection-ID lengths, the implementation offset can be compared directly with the formula.

requirements.condition: When calculating the base Packet Number field offset of a long-header packet
requirements.required_behavior: Compute pn_offset as 7 + len(destination_connection_id) + len(source_connection_id) + len(payload_length).
requirements.why_checkable: For long-header packets with varied encoded field lengths, the computed offset can be compared directly with the formula.

requirements.condition: When the long-header packet is an Initial packet
requirements.required_behavior: Add len(token_length) + len(token) to the base pn_offset.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the non-Initial long-header offset without accounting for the token fields.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial packets with different token encodings can be parsed and the resulting Packet Number offset checked against the conditional adjustment.

requirements.quote:
Multiple QUIC packets might be included in the same UDP datagram.
   Each packet is handled separately.
requirements.condition: When a UDP datagram contains multiple QUIC packets
requirements.required_behavior: Handle each QUIC packet separately, including its own header protection sample and processing state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat the coalesced packets as one packet for header protection sampling or packet processing.
requirements.why_checkable: A coalesced datagram can be supplied and per-packet parsing, sample selection, and processing outcomes observed independently.
